title: Login and data share one project
explanation: Supabase Auth and the Supabase database live in the same project, so your data security rules can check who is logged in directly.
builder: Protect every table with row-level security policies that use auth.uid().

title: File access can use who is logged in
explanation: Supabase Storage shares the project with Supabase Auth, so you can decide who sees each file based on the logged-in person.
builder: Protect storage buckets with policies that check the logged-in user.

title: Login and data share one project
explanation: Firestore security rules can check who is logged in with Firebase Auth directly, with no extra setup.
builder: Protect all data with Firestore security rules that check request.auth.

title: Clerk needs a one-time connection to Supabase
explanation: Supabase can accept Clerk logins, but you have to connect the two first. Until then, Supabase's data security rules can't tell who is logged in.
fix: Follow Supabase's third-party auth guide for Clerk before writing data rules.
builder: Configure Clerk as a third-party auth provider in Supabase before writing row-level security policies.

title: Firebase Auth needs a one-time connection to Supabase
explanation: Supabase can accept Firebase logins, but you have to connect the two first so data security rules know who is logged in. That's also two consoles to manage.
fix: Follow Supabase's third-party auth guide for Firebase Auth, or use Supabase Auth.
builder: Configure Firebase Auth as a third-party auth provider in Supabase before writing row-level security policies.

title: Made by the same team
explanation: Vercel builds Next.js, so new Next.js features usually work there first, with no extra setup.
